recent_articles.title: NCCIA uncovers gang selling data of govt officials to foreign entities; four arrested - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA)** arrested four individuals in South Punjab for selling sensitive personal data of government officers to foreign entities. The suspects, identified as Arshad Tariq, Arham Bari, Anam Sabir and Mohammad Rizwan, were allegedly sharing the data with foreign intelligence agencies.  **The NCCIA** is investigating how the information was accessed and has directed government institutions to strengthen data security.

recent_articles.title: Bolivia in crisis: Social unrest, demands for president to resign escalate | Protests News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rodrigo Paz**, Bolivia's president, is facing growing social unrest and demands for his resignation.  The protests began over a convergence of sector-based demands, including wage increases, contaminated fuel issues, and land classification changes. **Indigenous groups** from the highlands escalated the protests by blocking roads, demanding the president step down. Former President **Evo Morales**, who was ousted in 2019, has mobilized his supporters to pressure **President Paz**. The government is attempting to address legitimate demands while also cracking down on those deemed hostile to democracy.  The unrest has led to violence and clashes between protesters and police, with over 120 people detained.  **Jose Luis Lupo**, the Presidency Minister, stated that the government will use dialogue for legitimate sectors and full force of the law against those attacking democracy. The situation remains fluid as authorities seek a path forward.

recent_articles.title: Why is the US putting pressure on Cuba and what are Trump's aims?
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The United States is escalating pressure on Cuba, accusing the country of posing a national security threat and recently indicting former leader Raúl Castro. The US has imposed an oil blockade, sanctions, and a murder indictment against Castro, citing an incident in 1996 where Cuban fighter jets shot down two civilian planes owned by Cuban exiles.  Cuba maintains its actions were justified as self-defense within its airspace and accuses the US of using the charges to justify military aggression. The US has also targeted senior Cuban officials accused of human rights abuses or corruption, while offering $100 million in aid through humanitarian organizations. Cuba's response has been characterized by fiery rhetoric, with leaders demanding an end to the blockade and accusing the US of "coercion" and threats. China and Russia have condemned the US pressure on Cuba.

recent_articles.title: ACB books Medchal deputy collector in disproportionate assets case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB)** officials conducted searches on **Marri Vamshi Mohan**, a Special Grade Deputy Collector, and his associates following allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income. The searches uncovered properties valued at around ₹6.22 crore, including land plots, houses, and vehicles, along with cash and gold ornaments. **Vamshi Mohan** was arrested and remanded to judicial custody.  The investigation is ongoing.

recent_articles.title: Turkiye shutters liberal Istanbul university seized in criminal probe | Education News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Recep Tayyip Erdogan** revoked the operating license for Istanbul Bilgi University, a private university known for its liberal values, citing insufficient education standards. The closure, effective immediately, follows a criminal investigation into the institution's parent company and has sparked protests from students who will now continue their studies at Mimar Sinan University. **The Council of Higher Education** promised to ensure student safety during this transition.

recent_articles.title: Marco Rubio visits India: What’s at stake with Trump-Modi ties strained? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Marco Rubio**, US Secretary of State, is visiting India for a three-day trip ahead of the Quad meeting on May 26th.  Rubio's visit comes amidst strained relations between **Donald Trump** and **Narendra Modi**, as well as efforts to mend ties with **India**. The visit also coincides with the US Department of Justice dropping criminal fraud charges against Indian billionaire **Gautam Adani**, and an extension of a sanctions waiver allowing purchases of Russian oil.  Rubio's trip is seen as part of Washington's effort to strengthen bilateral relations with India, particularly in light of tensions between Trump and Modi last year.

recent_articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for gold scam in US, picked 16 gold bars from elderly victims - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Syed M Makki**, a 38-year-old Indian man, was sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for his role in a gold scam targeting elderly victims across the US.  The scheme involved malware that tricked victims into believing they were dealing with legitimate authorities, leading them to liquidate their savings and purchase gold bullion. **Makki** acted as a courier, collecting gold bars from victims and delivering them to co-conspirators. The Justice Department reported that the scam resulted in over $4.75 million in losses for victims.

recent_articles.title: Turkish opposition fights court ousting of leaders in ruling boosting Erdogan
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Turkish** opposition, led by Özgür Özel of the Republican People's Party (CHP), is challenging a court ruling removing them from leadership positions. The appeals court declared the 2023 leadership election null and void, prompting protests and criticism from opposition leaders who accuse President **Recep Tayyip Erdogan** of seeking to eliminate rivals.  The ruling has sparked concerns about the future of Turkey's political landscape and potential for snap elections.

recent_articles.title: Turkiye's Erdogan shuts Istanbul Bilgi University seized by state in criminal probe - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Turkey's** government revoked the operational license of **Istanbul Bilgi University**, forcing its closure, citing insufficient educational standards. The decision was made after the university was seized last year as part of a criminal investigation into **Can Holding**, which owned the institution.  The university, with over 20,000 students from Turkey and abroad, is known for its liberal politics and participation in the Erasmus exchange program.  Students will continue their studies at the Mimar Sinan University of Fine Arts, the university's guarantor school.

recent_articles.title: NCERT book row: SC modifies earlier order concerning 3 academics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** on Friday reversed its March 11 order that directed the Centre, States, and others to disassociate from three academics involved in a controversial chapter of the NCERT's Class 8 social science textbook. The court left it up to the Centre, states, universities, and institutions to make their own decisions regarding the issue without being influenced by its previous observations.  The Court also clarified that its comments were made in context of the content and not the individuals involved.

recent_articles.title: Turkish court ousts leader of main opposition party | Politics News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A Turkish court overturned the 2023 leadership election of the main opposition **Republican People’s Party (CHP)**, reinstating former chair Kemal Kilicdaroglu as interim leader. The ruling is seen as a move against the CHP, which won a significant victory over President **Recep Tayyip Erdogan**'s AK Party in the 2024 local elections and has been rising in polls. The CHP rejected the decision as an "attempted coup," while the government claimed it renewed faith in the rule of law.  The ruling sparked market turmoil, with the Borsa Istanbul index dropping 6 percent and government bonds sliding.

recent_articles.title: Friday briefing: ​As Israel’s coalition collapses, can its prime minister hang on to power? | Israel | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Israeli legislators voted to dissolve parliament and call for new elections. The move is largely attributed to the current coalition government's instability, with opposition parties gaining traction in recent polls.  Benjamin Netanyahu, currently facing trial for corruption charges, remains a strong contender but faces an uncertain future as his political landscape shifts. Public opinion has shifted towards more progressive views, creating a complex and unpredictable race for power.

recent_articles.title: Fake call centres duping U.S. citizens busted in Bengaluru, man from Delhi, another from U.P. arrested - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka State Cyber Command** officials raided four fake call centers in Bengaluru, uncovering a sophisticated operation that defrauded U.S. citizens by impersonating a prominent American accounting firm. The accused, Prashanth and Akash, allegedly collected millions of rupees from victims through fake tax advice, license renewal services, and counterfeit software keys.  The investigation revealed the use of shell companies to launder money and a network of over 120 employees trained to deceive victims using US accents. **Pronab Mohanty**, Director General of Cyber Command, stated that further investigations will focus on tracing the money trail and identifying bank accounts used in the fraud.

recent_articles.title: Assistant Director of Mines in Ranipet relieved of duties - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D. Mohan**, Director of Geology and Mining, relieved **E. Srinivasarao**, Assistant Director of the Ranipet office, of his duties due to allegations that he demanded ₹2 lakh in cash from a stone quarry operator to relax mining norms. The incident was reported to the Ministry of Natural Resources, Minerals and Mines, headed by Minister **T.K. Prabhu**.  **A. Arumuganainar**, Regional Joint Director of Geology and Mining (Villupuram), will now hold full additional charge of the post of AD of Geology and Mining for Ranipet district.

recent_articles.title: Imran’s cases will be fixed after Eid, CJP assures PTI - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi** assured **PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja** that the cases concerning access to a personal physician, family members and counsel for former premier Imran Khan would be scheduled after Eidul Azha.  Raja reported that the CJP had issued instructions to senior officers of the Supreme Court to fix these petitions. The PTI general secretary also stated that the appeals regarding Imran's access were pending before the SC since October 2025, and a petition by Imran's sister challenging the IHC ruling was also pending.  The **Supreme Court** disposed of appeals filed by the Punjab prosecution seeking cancellation of bail granted to **Ejaz Ahmed Chaudhry**, involved in the May 9 cases.

recent_articles.title: Who are the 10 best FIFA World Cup players of all time? | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Zinedine Zidane**, **Jimmy Greaves**, **Ferenc Puskas**, **Lothar Matthaus**, **Miroslav Klose**, **Ronaldo**, **Franz Beckenbauer**, **Johan Cruyff**, **Diego Maradona**, and **Pele** are considered among the best FIFA World Cup players of all time.  They have achieved success on the field, both individually and with their national teams. Some, like **Zidane**, **Greaves**, and **Beckenbauer**, have also been recognized for their leadership and contributions to the sport.

recent_articles.title: Who is Mohammed Omar, $90-million fraud suspect in Minnesota, who jumped from balcony to evade FBI arrest? - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohammed Omar**, charged with conspiracy to commit health care fraud and four counts of health care fraud, jumped from a fourth-floor balcony during an FBI arrest attempt in Minnesota on Thursday. **Colin McDonald**, Assistant Attorney General for the National Fraud Enforcement Division, urged the public to help capture Omar, who allegedly operated two companies, North Home Health Care and South Home Health Care, with Ibrahim Bashir Abdi to defraud the government of $90 million through falsified service hours. The scheme involved using disabled individuals as "lottery tickets" to generate millions of dollars for luxury purchases.

recent_articles.title: Parody Cockroach Janta political party’s rise reflects youth anger in India | India | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A satirical online movement, the Cockroach Janta (People's) party, has gained significant traction in India.  **Abhijeet Dipke**, a political communications strategist and student at Boston University, founded the movement after **Surya Kant**, the Supreme Court chief justice, sparked backlash with comments comparing unemployed young people to cockroaches. The CJP uses absurdist humor to mock corruption, joblessness, and government dysfunction, attracting millions of followers on social media.  While some dismiss it as a digital gimmick, Dipke believes it reflects mounting frustration among India's youth and could lead to real political change.

recent_articles.title: Cubans outraged at US charges against Raúl Castro but view military strikes as serious possibility | Cuba | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The US has indicted former Cuban president Raúl Castro on charges related to the 1996 shooting down of two unarmed planes belonging to the Brothers to the Rescue group. The indictment, which follows weeks of heightened tensions between the two countries, comes amidst increased surveillance and military activity in the region.  **Marco Rubio**, **US Secretary of State**, has offered aid to Cuba while also blaming the Cuban government for the ongoing blackouts and economic hardship. Concerns about US attempts to exert control over Cuba have been raised by some, particularly in light of recent reports suggesting a potential deal between Sherritt, a major Cuban nickel miner, and a former Trump advisor.

recent_articles.title: I am from India but none of my firm partners is Indian: Attorney Rahul Reddy counters hate on social media - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Reddy**, an immigration attorney, and **Emily Neumann**, a partner at his firm, the Reddy-Neumann Brown PC, addressed concerns about the "Indians only hire Indians" narrative circulating on social media. They emphasized that while fraud exists within the H-1B program, it does not represent the entire process or all individuals involved.  **Dr. Sean Wang**, a Chinese-American assistant professor, also filed a lawsuit against **Southern Methodist University**, alleging preferential treatment of Indian employees by head of the department **Dr. Hemang Desai**.

recent_articles.title: ‘It’s broken English’: MP’s attempt to speak Jamaican in parliament sparks language row | Jamaica | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A Jamaican MP, Nekeisha Burchell, sparked controversy in parliament when she spoke in Jamaican Patois during her maiden speech. **Juliet Holness**, the speaker of the house and wife of Jamaica's prime minister, interrupted her, citing parliamentary rules requiring English language use. The incident ignited debate about the legacy of British colonialism and whether Jamaica should embrace its own language in formal settings.  **Marlon Morgan**, a parliamentary secretary, argued for a more thoughtful approach to any potential change in language usage within parliament, while others like **Carolyn Cooper**, a literary scholar, supported Burchell's intervention as a symbol of cultural confidence. The issue has sparked public debate about the legitimacy and use of Jamaican Patois in Jamaica.

recent_articles.title: Canada is using its borders to police Palestine solidarity | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Canada** is increasingly scrutinizing individuals critical of Israel's actions in Gaza, including scholars and speakers invited to the Muslim Association of Canada’s annual convention.  These incidents include visa revocations, interrogations at airports, and denials of entry. **HonestReporting Canada**, **B’nai Brith Canada**, and other pro-Israel groups have been actively campaigning against these individuals and events. This trend reflects a wider pattern in Western nations where governments are increasingly using immigration law, surveillance powers, and institutional pressure to silence dissent on political issues.  This raises concerns about the erosion of democratic principles and the potential for broader suppression of dissenting voices.

recent_articles.title: CM’s appeal to kids for votes: Plea in Madras High Court seeks an inquiry by Election Commission - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: DMK, AIADMK, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Election Commission of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition has been filed in the Madras High Court, seeking an inquiry by the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** into allegations of electoral malpractice during the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The petitioner, L. Vasuki, argues that **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay**'s appeal to children to vote for his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), constitutes "exploitation of minor children for electoral propaganda" and falls under the definition of corrupt practice.  The petition also cites a representation by the anti-corruption organization Arappor Iyakkam alleging that **DMK** and **AIADMK** members distributed cash to voters in certain constituencies. The court has sought responses from the **ECI** and **CEO** by May 29, 2026.

recent_articles.title: 5 Indians, 2 US businessmen: Inside India's call center operation that FBI shut down for fraud - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The FBI shut down a call center operation in India that defrauded hundreds of elderly victims across the US and elsewhere. **Adam Young** and **Harrison Gevirtz**, two former CEOs of a telecommunications company, Ringba, pleaded guilty to misprision of a felony for their role in enabling the scam. The investigation revealed that Indian citizens Sahil Narang, Chirag Sachdeva, Abrar Anjum, Manish Kumar, and Jagmeet Singh Virk were convicted of similar charges. **The FBI** is urging consumers to be aware of tech support scams and report any suspicious activity.

recent_articles.title: Israel pushes for war amid US ceasefire, but its options may be limited | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Israel's** political establishment is reportedly eager to restart hostilities with **Iran**, despite a US ceasefire.  While **Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu** faces pressure from both the public and opposition leaders to resume the conflict, it is unlikely he can do so without **US permission**.  The recent ceasefire has proven politically costly for **Netanyahu**, who is facing criticism for his handling of the situation.  However, some analysts believe that **Netanyahu** may be motivated by a desire to secure a strategic victory and boost his chances in upcoming elections.  Ultimately, the decision to resume conflict will likely hinge on US approval.

recent_articles.title: Ketan Parekh Case: Sebi sends show cause notice to 6 Capital Group FPIs - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sebi** has initiated legal proceedings against **Capital Group**, alleging that its traders, James Vincent Cheng and Terence Tsai, leaked sensitive information about impending trades to Salgaocar, who then shared it with Ketan Parekh for front-running the market. The regulator claims that this resulted in illicit gains for those involved.  The investigation covers a period from January 1, 2021, to June 20, 2023, and Sebi alleges that **Capital Group** failed to maintain confidentiality regarding its trading intentions.

recent_articles.title: US police officers sue Trump over $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Two US police officers, Harry Dunn and Daniel Hodges, have filed a lawsuit against the **Trump** administration alleging that its $1.776 billion "anti-weaponisation" fund will be used to compensate January 6th rioters. The officers argue that the fund is a form of presidential corruption and will encourage further violence by rewarding those who attacked the US Capitol.  The lawsuit seeks to dissolve the fund, claiming it allows for taxpayer money to be disbursed to participants in the attack on January 6th, 2021.

recent_articles.title: I tried to buy a Cambridge paper online, this is what happened - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: This summer, leaked Cambridge International Examinations (CAIE) papers have caused widespread disruption for Pakistani students.  **Cambridge Assessment International Education (CAIE**) reported the theft and unauthorized sharing of examination papers on May 7th and 14th, with evidence being sent to platforms where the leaks circulated. The agency is investigating both incidents thoroughly through digital forensics, analysis of online platforms, and cooperation with law enforcement. **Anant Nanda**, an A Level student from Lahore, discovered a Discord server called "Cambridge Leaks" that sells leaked papers for $100 each.  He attempted to purchase a Mathematics Paper 1 exam paper, which was available on the website for sale. The CAIE has assured students and schools that it is working to protect them from this problem. Parents are concerned about fair assessments and the future of their children's education.

recent_articles.title: US indicts Cuba’s former leader Raul Castro: Why it matters | Raul Castro News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **United States** has indicted former Cuban leader Raul Castro on charges of conspiracy to kill US nationals, murder, and aircraft destruction. The indictment stems from the 1996 shooting down of two planes operated by a Cuban exile group, Brothers to the Rescue, killing four Americans. This move follows a pattern of US criminal cases targeting foreign leaders, including Venezuela's **Nicolas Maduro**, and comes amid escalating tensions between Cuba and the US.  The Trump administration has imposed sanctions on Cuba and threatened military action if its demands for regime change are not met. However, some analysts believe the indictment is part of a broader strategy to pressure Cuba's government through economic reforms rather than regime change.

recent_articles.title: Trump endorses Ken Paxton in Texas, gambling on a challenger with baggage in a crucial race
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** endorsed **Ken Paxton**, Texas Attorney General, in his bid to unseat incumbent Senator John Cornyn. This move dismayed many Senate Republicans who view Paxton as a controversial figure with political baggage.  Trump's endorsement is part of a pattern of supporting challengers against Republican incumbents, and it could significantly impact the outcome of the upcoming primary election. The winner will face Democrat James Talarico in November's general election.

recent_articles.title: Austrian ex-intelligence officer found guilty of Russia spying charges
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Egisto Ott**, a former Austrian intelligence officer, has been found guilty of spying for Russia and other charges. A jury in Vienna sentenced him to four years and one month in prison after finding him guilty of providing information to Russian intelligence officers and fugitive executive **Jan Marsalek**.  The case has raised concerns about the potential for continued Russian espionage activity within Austria. Prosecutors allege that Ott, who denies the charges, received payment from **Marsalek** for his actions. The investigation into **Marsalek**, also an Austrian citizen wanted by German authorities, is ongoing.

recent_articles.title: Sebi proposes to permit third-party payment in mutual funds in certain scenarios - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sebi**, the Indian markets regulator, proposed allowing third-party payments in mutual funds for specific scenarios such as employer-sponsored investments and AMC payment of commissions. The proposals aim to balance ease of investing with investor protection by implementing safeguards like KYC checks and electronic fund trails. **Sebi** seeks public comments on these changes until June 10th.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Colorado governor faces backlash over clemency for 2020 election denier Tina Peters
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Governor Jared Polis** of Colorado faced criticism from fellow Democrats and some Republicans after commuting the prison sentence of former county clerk **Tina Peters**, a 2020 election denier convicted of tampering with election equipment.  **Secretary of State Jena Griswold** called the decision "an affront to our democracy", while **President Donald Trump** praised Peters' release on social media. **Peters** expressed remorse for her actions, but Governor Polis defended his commutation by arguing that her sentence was disproportionate for a first-time offender.

recent_articles.title: Zimbabwe’s diaspora reshapes real estate and farming investment trends | Features | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Zimbabwean** digital influencers, Kundai Chitima and Kelvin Birioti, are influencing diaspora investment decisions through their social media content.  Their videos highlight opportunities in real estate, farming, and market trends, prompting some diaspora members to reconsider returning or investing in Zimbabwe. **Nyashadzashe Nguwo**, an Africa market entry advisor based in the UK, states that many individuals are relocating due to a combination of emotional and lifestyle-driven factors, including a desire to reconnect with their roots and contribute to national development.  **Catherine Mutisi**, a diaspora member who had previously invested in Zimbabwe, credits social media content for shifting her perspective on returning permanently. Economic pressures, such as high unemployment rates and rising living costs, continue to influence migration decisions, but the strong economic link between **Zimbabwe** and its diaspora remains significant, with diaspora investment playing a crucial role in various sectors.

recent_articles.title: Andalucíans to vote in election seen as gauge of Spain’s wider political change | Spain | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming election in Andalucía, Spain's most populous region, is expected to deliver an absolute majority for the conservative People’s Party (PP) and further weaken the Socialists. **Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla**, the PP regional president, seeks to capitalize on scandals surrounding Prime Minister **Pedro Sánchez** and his administration.  The PP aims to portray the election as a referendum on Sánchez's leadership, while Vox is expected to gain seats. The outcome will have implications for Spain's upcoming general election next year.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Cabinet portfolios: CM Vijay to hold Home; Finance for Sengottaiyan; Aadhav Arjuna gets PWD - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, has announced the portfolios for his cabinet members. **Vijay** will oversee key departments including Home, Police, and IAS/IPS officers.  **N. Anand**, the deputy chief minister, will handle Rural Development and Water Resources. Other ministers have been assigned specific responsibilities in areas such as health, education, finance, and energy. The Governor has approved the recommendations.

recent_articles.title: Arrest of Iraqi terror suspect with alleged links to Iran’s Quds Force is astonishing but not surprising | Iran | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An alleged Iraqi commander of an Iranian-backed militia group, **Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi**, has been arrested in the US on charges of orchestrating 18 terrorist attacks across Europe and Canada since the beginning of the Iran war. The complaint alleges that al-Saadi is responsible for a string of recent firebombings, an arson attack on a synagogue, and a shooting at the US consulate in Toronto, as well as a wave of attacks on Jewish targets in the UK.  Al-Saadi allegedly posted claims of responsibility for attacks on social media platforms under the name of **Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia (HAYI)**, a group believed to be linked to the **Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)**. The arrest comes as no surprise to investigators and analysts who have long suspected Iranian involvement in these attacks.

recent_articles.title: Palestinian leaders hold rare party meeting as polls show rising discontent
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mahmoud Abbas**, the 90-year-old Palestinian President, was re-elected as head of **Fatah** at its first major conference in a decade.  The meeting comes amid rising discontent among Palestinians, with polls indicating widespread dissatisfaction and calls for Abbas' resignation. The conference aims to address these concerns and implement reforms, but critics point out internal divisions and nepotism within the party.  Despite promises of elections and unity, many Palestinians feel that **Fatah** has lost its way and is prioritizing its own interests over those of the Palestinian people.

recent_articles.title: Where did Eurovision go wrong? | Music News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Eurovision Song Contest, a major global entertainment event, is facing controversy due to Israel's participation.  **Israel’s President Isaac Herzog**, and the **Israeli Broadcasting Authority (Kan)** have spent significant resources promoting Israel's presence in the contest, while artists and broadcasters are boycotting it. Critics argue that Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide and question the event's ability to remain apolitical.  The EBU has defended its decision, citing Kan's independence from the Israeli government, but critics point out a perceived double standard compared to Russia's ban following its invasion of Ukraine. The controversy has led to boycotts by broadcasters in several countries, including the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, Iceland, and Ireland, while artists like **Molly Nilsson** have called for a boycott until Israel is removed.  The financial impact of these boycotts is significant, with some estimates suggesting that it could remove millions of euros from the contest's funding pool.
